name: Plitvice Lakes
title: Holidays in Plitvice Lakes
intro: Sixteen terraced lakes linked by waterfalls and wooden boardwalks in a forested national park. Here's what the Plitvice Lakes are like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June, September and October are best, with full waterfalls and fewer crowds. July and August are very busy, so book timed tickets and arrive early. In winter some trails and the boats close, but snowy waterfalls are beautiful.

things.name: Lower Lakes
things.blurb: Boardwalks lead to Veliki Slap, Croatia's tallest waterfall. The park ticket covers all the trails.

things.name: Upper Lakes
things.blurb: Wooden paths zigzag across lakes and cascades. Quieter than the Lower Lakes later in the day.

things.name: Kozjak boat
things.blurb: An electric boat crosses the biggest lake, included in the park ticket and a welcome rest for small legs.

things.name: Panoramic train
things.blurb: A road train links the entrances and the upper lakes, also included in the ticket.

things.name: Rastoke
things.blurb: A village of old water mills and little waterfalls in Slunj, about half an hour north.

things.name: Barać Caves
things.blurb: Guided tours through caves near Rakovica, a good choice on a rainy day.

faqs.question: Are Plitvice Lakes good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, as part of a Croatia trip. Children love the boardwalks and waterfalls, and the routes have boats and trains to rest on. Boardwalks have no railings in places, so hold hands with little ones.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: One or two nights nearby lets you visit early before the crowds. Most families combine it with the coast at Zadar or Split.

faqs.question: How do you get there from the UK?
faqs.answer: Fly to Zagreb or Zadar, then drive about two hours. A hire car is easiest, though buses stop at the park. British passport holders can visit for up to 90 days in any 180 without a visa. New EU entry checks are being brought in, so check GOV.UK before you travel.

faqs.question: Can you swim in the lakes?
faqs.answer: No, swimming is banned in the park. Head to the coast or a lake outside the park to cool off.
